decision_framework.title: Frontend State Architecture Selection Matrix
decision_framework.context: Selecting the appropriate state storage tier when introducing new stateful logic in React / Next.js applications.

branch.condition: State alters the primary visual dataset, requires bookmarking, browser back/forward, or link sharing (e.g. search keywords, active filters, pagination page, tab selection)
branch.trade_offs: State survives page refresh and is 100% shareable; trade-off: serialized as string, requires debounce on high-frequency text input.
branch.anti_pattern: Never store page numbers or active tab IDs purely in React useState.

branch.condition: State represents asynchronous data fetched from server APIs that needs caching, deduplication, background polling, or optimistic updates
branch.recommendation: Server State (TanStack Query or React Server Components)
branch.trade_offs: Automates garbage collection and revalidation; trade-off: asynchronous, requires explicit 5-state UI handling.
branch.anti_pattern: Never duplicate server lists or entities into global Zustand stores.

branch.condition: State represents purely ephemeral user input being validated before submission
branch.recommendation: Form State (React Hook Form with Zod Resolver)
branch.trade_offs: Zero re-renders on keystroke, isolated component state; trade-off: local to form lifecycle.
branch.anti_pattern: Do not lift form input field values into global app state.

branch.condition: State represents global client-only UI flags (e.g. sidebar collapse, active theme, global command palette open/close)
branch.trade_offs: Instant synchronous access across any client component with zero boilerplate; trade-off: lost on hard refresh unless explicitly synced with localStorage.
branch.anti_pattern: Do not use Zustand for tabular server data.
